statement: You are given an m × n matrix in which no two adjacent cells hold the same value. A peak is a cell strictly greater than each of its neighbours above, below, left and right. Treat everything outside the matrix as −1, so border cells only have to beat the neighbours they actually have.
Find any peak and return its position as [row, column]. If there are several peaks, any one of them is accepted.

The search should run in O(m log n) or O(n log m) time. Binary search over the columns: in the middle column take the row of its largest value, then compare that cell with its left and right neighbours. If a neighbour is larger, a peak must exist on that side; otherwise the cell is a peak.

examples.explanation: 9, at row 2, column 2, is larger than 6 above it and 8 to its left, so it is a peak.
30 beats 20, 16, 21 and 14, so [1, 1] is a peak. 32 at [2, 2] is also a peak, and either answer would be accepted.

constraints: No two adjacent cells are equal
